title: access_counter wrapping inverts LRU eviction order after 2^64 operations
description:
**File:** rust/lichen-link/src/link_layer.rs
**Lines:** 328, 483, 684

**Issue:** access_counter uses wrapping_add(1). After 2^64 increments, the counter wraps to 0. Peers with access values near u64::MAX will appear 'older' than peers accessed at counter=1, inverting eviction order.

**Trigger:** System runs for extremely long time or processes ~10^19 frames. Practically impossible in current usage, but the semantic is wrong.

**Bad behavior:** After wrap, LRU eviction evicts recently-accessed peers instead of least-recently-accessed.

**Suggested fix:** Either: (1) accept as won't-happen in practice and document, (2) use saturating_add and treat MAX as 'always recent', or (3) periodically renumber all access values to compress the range. Option 1 is likely sufficient with a code comment.
close_reason: Replaced wrapping_add with saturating_add at all three access_counter sites (ReplayProtector::check_and_update, LinkLayer::add_peer, LinkLayer::receive_frame) and documented saturation semantics on both structs and evict_if_needed: after u64::MAX, new accesses tie with the most-recent tier, degrading eviction to arbitrary-among-newest instead of inverting LRU order. Tests seed access_counter near u64::MAX and prove the pre-saturation oldest peer is evicted while saturated newest peers survive, for both ReplayProtector and LinkLayer.
